projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Wallace Cavett was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ___+ Wallace. ?Actually, did I say that right --?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Wallace Eugene Cavett.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, and the state of North Carolina is where you currently reside. Today is July 22nd, 2003. Date of birth is October ?5th?, 1922 and if you just want to get started, sir, were you drafted or did you enlist, or just go from there --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I enlisted.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Enlisted, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. What did you enlist in and what are you reasons for that?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Well I enlisted -- enlisted in 1942.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: And the war was on. World War I -- II was on, and I decided to -- I finished my high school and two years of college, and I figured I was going to be -- go into the military. Everybody was doing, so I figured I might as well, too. So I got -- I go into the ?first -- first? -- funny story on this this now. I went into the -- ___ New Mexico -- yeah, New Mexico. I went in. I was going to join the Air Force. But I couldn't pass -- I didn't pass the exam to get in the Air Force. I went across the street and joined the Marines. {Laughs.}

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: How come?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Been a marine ever since. But, I -- as soon as I got through that, they sent me to flight school. I went to flight school, and I left -- when they sent me to flight school to Jacksonville, Florida to go through what they call a ?dash drive?.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Now, about how you enlisted, did you --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: No, I was -- I was an officer then.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You were an officer then?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: And later on I was ___+ when I enlisted?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. So you went the advanced flight.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I went to advanced flight, and when I got out of there I -- I went about the time when World War II was over and they reverted us all back. They reverted me back to Master Sergeant. I was a Senior Master Sergeant in the Marine Corps. ?They had arranged? was 1938, ___+ give me ___+ was going to stay a Master Sergeant for 16 years. ___ right, Master Sergeant for 16 years. And then I made CW 01, and they made me CW 01, and I went on up through the ranks all the way to CW 04. And then, when I retired in 1973, they reverted me to -- back to First Lieutenant. What I had in World War II, First Lieutenant, so I had to go back to First Lieutenant.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Now, you were -- you were -- you saw -- you were in World War II, Korea and Vietnam.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You want to talk about your World War II experience?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I didn't have too much experience in World War II. I was flying. First thing -- first thing, I was there flying off a carrier, which was called the ?Scow Parow?, the Prow, the U.S.S. Prow and we called it the ?Scrow Prow?. It's a -- it's a jeep carrier. One of the first jeep carriers we came out with. And I was flying Corsairs then. And I was flying -- we were flying near and around -- I don't remember just how much -- that's -- that's my problem there I don't remember whereabouts we went, there. Maybe we gone in by the South Pacific, but we -- well, trying to think of the name of the ___+ down there, and we -- Mariner the closest ___ send us back to the 'States, so we were still on the ?Scow Parow?. When I got back to the 'States they took me off the ___ and put me on the ___ ... (3 seconds), which was nothing. I mean, you get -- they didn't even have -- they had one building, which was the only building they had. One building, then, was the one where they had the tower. That was the only building there, and we -- we slept in tents, and, in fact, I spent a -- I spent a hurricane in those tents. And I -- in fact, I was in charge -- everybody else left and they made me ___ in charge of as much as ___ ... (2 seconds) flew all the airplanes out they could fly, and both of them that couldn't fly, and we had to sleep there. And they made me in charge of it. And the water got so deep, that we had to ___+ waste water to get to where they had the ___ camp. ___ ... (2 seconds) and then we went back to this other camp that was a little bit higher, so that's where we slept. That took -- that went on for -- oh, it was over in -- of course, a hurricane ain't last very long, which is the rest of the ___ ... (2 seconds) somewhere I can't remember where it was, but I went out -- oh, I know where it is now. They sent me up to New York. Put me in the turret Command. And I was flying Corsairs in the ___ Command, and I was flying all over the United States and then eventually flew up to Europe. But after then -- after I came back, they put me -- put me in F9Fs, the jets. And they sent me to Korea, and I was flying -- in Korea, I was flying in the F9F jets, and I got shot down twice over there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ___ ... (8 seconds) So you got actually -- you actually got shot down, there?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Wow. So you survived.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: ___ ... (4 seconds). I didn't go down in flame, or anything like that --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: -- but I -- at full throttle, I could give 157 miles ___+ and you start out at 150. So -- so evidently, I was able to control it going to the ground.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Is that the only time you got shot down?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Is that the only time --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: That's the only time I was really shot down, but I -- the first 54 missions I had over there -- 20, 30, wait -- 42 of them come back full of bullet holes in the planes.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: 42 of them?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: 42 of them, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: That's a ___ ... (2 seconds)?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: ___ ... (3 seconds) I didn't get beat up for nothing ___+.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So you had to have been concerned. I mean, every time you went out?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you just to think about it, or?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You just did your job --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: It's my only job to do.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ?Only job to do? That's amazing. Had a lot of good friends there, didn't you?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Sorry?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Probably had a lot of good friends over there, didn't you?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Oh, yeah. Yeah, a bunch of them. Yeah. Most of them are gone now, of course, but I had a lot of them over there that were flying with me.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was Korea the most intense?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was Korea the most intense fighting?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah. There, I had to do 117 missions in Korea. In fact, I got the Standard Flying Cross for blowing up one of the Korean's ammunition dumps, and I had to fly in through all this incoming --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ___ yeah?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: And blew up this ammunition dump, and they gave me the Standard Flying Cross for that. And then I -- I blew up -- well, most of the time, what we were doing was either strafing trenches or blowing up bridges and stuff like that. But, it was -- I don't know, it's kind of -- I don't remember all of it. My memory's not like it used to be.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: It's all right. It's incredible. All right, so then, is that all of Korea, is that basically what you did? You just did a lot of missions and --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: -- and then you left that and but you stayed in?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Well, I left that and came back to the 'States and then, I got married. And five months after I got married, they sent me to Vietnam. {Laughs.}

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Oh, man. What did you think when you got to Vietnam?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Well, it was -- actually, it was -- it was -- like it -- I thought it was very stupid because they weren't using enough force, and the Vietnamese was not that good at fighting. I mean, they put you in there and ___+ and two of these places there, and I was -- at that time, I was -- I was flying the helicopters. We'd fly helicopters. We'd go out and pick up scouting teams if they got bind in where they couldn't get out we'd go and pick them up. And I got a joke on that. I don't know whether you'd want that or not but --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: That's fine.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: The -- this one place we went into, I told my crew chief, my copilot, I says, "As soon as we land," -- because we'd already taken ___, we'd already taken shots -- this is funny -- soon as we land, I said -- Dr. Ramford says, "?Come on in? or get out of here." So we get down, ___+ and Dr. Ramford and they come aboard. And I hollered at the boy, I said, "Pick up the ramp." And he just looked at me. And I kept hollering at him, "Pick up the ramp," and he didn't do it, so I had to reach way over and pick up the ramp myself. I got out of there and got up out of the fire, and I asked him, I said, "How come you didn't pick up the ramp?" He says, "I don't bother you when you're having a bowel movement."

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: {Laughs.}

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Then I was flying -- I was flying the R4Ds in parachutes, dropping parachute people on the ground. So I come back from over there. Then I got around one of the fires that blew up in the back engine, and I had to nose-dive that to get it back on the ground before it burned up. I got it back on the ground, and we got out of it. And, my crew chief was smart enough that he -- he pushed it out. I hung along the side and I said, "Oh, boy. It's going to burn, this." But the darn thing didn't burn the plane at all. It didn't burn it at all. It burned out before we got back to -- back where we landed, so it --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Was that a helicopter?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: No, it's an R4D.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: R4D?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Transport plane, yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. But you did fly helicopters, too?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah, I flew helicopters ___+ when I first went over there, I went over there flying the CS33s, which is the big heavy transports. And we flew ___+ most of the -- then they didn't have anybody to fly the R4D for ___, so they pulled my out of there and put me ___+ {laughs}.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So you -- you could fly just about anything over there?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah. I had the fly the -- had to fly the flare ships for them because they -- I would say 90 percent of our -- our work over there was at night, and flare ships are -- you drop the flare, and they could see what they were -- they were doing over there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: All right.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: So that's mostly what I did there in the last six months I was over there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Do you have any specific stories that you want to tell, or?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah, not really.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: -- any incidents that were important

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah. Don't have any stories {laughs}.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Well, talk about these pictures. You got some amazing pictures. You still talk to any of these people? Are any of these people still around, or --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: No, I don't think so. No, these people -- I know they are all gone. This was my crew that's in Corsairs.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Corsairs?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Here and here.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay. And that's the damage --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: ___+ ?in the nose? over there.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: He got shot down. That's amazing.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I hope some of these people are still alive, but I haven't any of them in a long time, so I don't know.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ___+ school?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I was up at the Oregon school, but they didn't catch up at ___+.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Okay, ___?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: ___ ... (3 seconds) A lot of your time was spent training, wasn't it?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: This was -- that's where we checked out in the F 80s. Where I -- ___.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What all different types of aircraft did you fly?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Sorry?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What were all the types of aircraft that you flew?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Jeez, I don't know.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: It's that many, huh?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I flew quite a few of them. I don't remember. There's a picture of an F80 there, too.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So what did you decide to do -- what did you do after you got out of the military?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: What did you do after you got out of the military?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Well, I had a nephew that was in a -- a marine business, and he wanted me to go in with him, so I went in with him. And about a year later he wasn't making enough money, so he I bought it off of him and I still got it. I'm running it. C and H Marine on West ___ Road.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: I see you kept your -- some of your fly records and stuff. Is that like --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah, they all -- all in -- not all of them, because it's -- in Korea there are the -- the operation office burnt down and blew up -- burnt up a couple of them.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Oh, is that right?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You lost your --

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: All I've got here is six -- yeah, six of them.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And that just details your flight times and what you do and --

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: So you went through ___ and, of course, that changes quite a bit, I imagine?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: And what you did. That's a good thing to keep.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah, these things are -- some of these are 50 years old.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you have anything you did for good luck, or?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Do what now?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Did you have anything you did for good luck or superstitions or anything?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I really don't have that much superstitions. You either did or you didn't {laughs}.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Yeah. Is there anything outside -- you belong to some -- obviously, you belong to some veterans' organizations?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You belong to some veterans' organizations and stuff?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Just about everyone that is out there: life member of the American Legion, life member of the BFW, life member of the DAV, life member of the DD

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I'm also chairman of Clark County's Veterans' Council.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I'm around a few of them.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: That's quite a list. Did you go back to school? Did you take advantage of the GI bill or anything like that?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: No, I didn't go back to school. I figured I was to old, time I got out in '73.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: You went for so -- so many years?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: All right, well. Is there anything you wanted to add?

sp.speaker: Wallace Cavett
sp.p: I don't know ___+ I hope -- I hope it's -- I hope it's done you some good.

sp.speaker: Jason Lowry
sp.p: Oh, absolutely. It's a great story. I mean you have a lot of a -- a lot of experience. So what I'll do is go.
